new_statements.quote: [p.51] ... un seul noyau accentué, ainsi qu'un satellite postnucléaire optionnel. Le composé par contre contient plus d'un seul noyau dont chacun a un accent primaire [...]. En minyanka cette distinction entre mot de base et mot composé est semblable. Lorsqu'on parle de syllabe accentuée il s'agit en général d'une syllabe initiale de radical. [p.52] En minyanka le choix des variantes des phonèmes consonantiques est lié au placement de l'accent. Dans le cas du phonème /g/ la réalisation [g] est donc réservée à une syllabe accentuée, donc à une syllabe initiale de radical [...] [p.100] Dans les composés et les dérivés chaque première syllabe de radical porte un accent. 2. Une telle syllabe accentuée a le même rang qu'une syllabe initiale de mot
new_statements.translation: [p.51] (the base word has) a single accented nucleus plus an optional post-nuclear satellite. The compound, by contrast, contains more than one nucleus, each with a primary accent [...]. In Minyanka this distinction between base word and compound is similar. When one speaks of the accented syllable, it is in general a radical-initial (root-initial) syllable. [p.52] In Minyanka the choice of consonant allophones is tied to the placement of the accent. For /g/, the realisation [g] is thus restricted to an accented syllable, i.e. a root-initial syllable [...] [p.100] In compounds and derivatives each first syllable of a root bears an accent. 2. Such an accented syllable has the same rank as a word-initial syllable.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Accent falls on the first syllable of the lexical root (radical); in a simple word (root + class suffix) this is the word-initial syllable, the class suffix being an unaccented post-nuclear 'satellite'. Compounds and derivatives carry one accent on the initial syllable of each root (transcriptions also mark derivational prefixes ta-, ka- as accented: ['ta'kana], ['ka'ce:ye]). Accent placement conditions consonant allophony ([g], [d] etc. only syllable-initially in accented = root-initial syllables). Corroborated first-hand by Coulibaly 2020:47 for Pénesso Minyanka: nominal class suffix -Ci (sonorant C) 'est toujours non-accentuée, et i est prononcé de façon très brève', and by Prost 1964:126 (unaccented class pronouns have e reduced to ə).
new_statements.secondary_stress: No primary/secondary ranking given in the accessible text: complex words simply 'peuvent porter plus d'un seul accent par mot', each root-initial syllable (and, per the transcriptions, derivational prefixes ta-/ka-) bearing 'un accent primaire'; the class suffix / post-nuclear satellite is unaccented.
new_statements.exceptions: Hedged 'en général'. p.52 nàgoo [nà'go:] 'enfants' is transcribed with accent on the second syllable (presumably nà- treated as a separate element). Loanwords from Bambara integrated as compounds show 'accent double' and deviant tone schemes (p.110). Coulibaly 2020:47 restricts his explicit 'non-accentuée' remark to class suffixes with a non-obstruent consonant and vowel i.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level accent in a tone language (3 tones in Yorosso/Mpessoba per Dombrowsky-Hahn; 2 tones in Pénesso per Coulibaly). Domain is the root/base within the phonological word ('mot de base' = one accented nucleus + unaccented satellite; 'composé' = several nuclei). Statements are distributional/phonotactic (accent licenses the full consonant inventory, vowel harmony copies the accented vowel), not instrumental. Dialects: Yorosso and Mpessoba (Sikasso region).
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe varieties of Mamara Senoufo / Minyanka [myk], glottocode mama1271 (no dialect-level glottocodes used). Dombrowsky-Hahn 1999 (the accent statement) describes the parlers of Yorosso and Mpessoba (Sikasso region, 3 tones). Coulibaly 2020/2023 describes the parler of Pénesso, cercle de Bla (Ségou region; 2 tones, heavy Bambara contact; author notes low intelligibility with the 'Mamara' of Carlson 1994). Prost 1964 describes Karangasso ('Mambar'); Chéron 1921/1925 the Koutiala variety. Mills 1984 (named by the earlier scan) is about Cebaara/Senadi Senoufo, not Mamara, and was not pursued.

sources.note: Ch.1 Phonologie (pp.37-63) covers consonants, vowels, tones (2 tones H/L + contours + downstep, §1.3) and syllable structure (§1.4); there is no section on accent. Only remark, p.47 (PDF p.48): 'La structure des suffixes nominaux de classe est CV en minyanka; lorsque C est une non-obstruante, et que V est i, la syllabe est toujours non-accentuée, et i est prononcé de façon très brève : kólì, cɛ̰́lí, ɲɛ̰́nì, sómì, fáyí'. p.74 quotes Dombrowsky-Hahn (1999:69) on vowel harmony copying 'la voyelle figurant dans la syllabe accentuée' of the base. No placement rule of its own.
